headline: 🔴 A FOURTH AGENT WALKED 2368 RIDGE TRAIL THURSDAY AND FILED THE HARSHEST FORM THIS BOARD HAS EVER TAKEN — not interested, too high, staging rated 1 of 5, and the reason was “too much work and unknowns.” ⭐ That is now FOUR independent reads saying too high on one address, plus a named buyer who put his own number on it — and the agent handed you a cheaper fix than a price cut: a pre-inspection. ⚠️ Everything else on this board is a call you already owe: Amy G. on day eight at 355 Comanche, the Fieldstone buyer's agent waiting since Wednesday, and the “VERY interested” buyer at 821 Martinwood, now twelve days cold.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 STILL THE BEST BUYER READ ON THE BOARD AND NOW ON DAY EIGHT. Amy G. of Ethos International filed interested — YES, and wrote that her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the TOP of their list. She left the price question BLANK. She is also the agent who phoned from inside the house mid-showing about the garage — and reported that the basement lights would not come on.
hotSignals.action: Call her, don't write. Answer the basement lights first — buyers who have just started looking are touring other homes this week with a dark basement as their last memory of yours. Then ask the question her blank price field invites: what would it take.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 NOT A SHOWINGTIME FORM — THE BUYER HIMSELF, BY TEXT. Adin D. named his gap under the ask, told you to save his number as a standing investor, and added “Happy to have you represent me.” Two days on, both of his questions — is there room, and will you represent me — are still unanswered.
hotSignals.action: One call does both jobs. And his number is now the best-supported figure on this house: Thursday's form made it four independent reads calling the price too high.

hotSignals.signal: 🆕 THE BUYER'S AGENT ASKED YOU TO PICK UP AND NOBODY HAS. Robert B. texted “let me know when you have a second” at 4:14 PM Wednesday, eight minutes after emailing that he would speak with his buyers about the inspection response you delivered at 1:21 PM. An agent who writes and then immediately asks for the phone is carrying an answer.
hotSignals.action: Call him this morning — it is now two days old, so the second call is yours to make. While you have him, close the item nobody has chased: the appraisal status with the lender.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE STRONGEST SINGLE WORD ANY AGENT HAS FILED ON THIS BOARD, AND IT IS TWELVE DAYS OLD. Wanda W. of Millennium Homes answered the interest question with the single word “Very” and left every other field blank. Two other agents toured the same weekend and both passed on SIZE, not price — verified three ways.
hotSignals.action: Call her. It is a team listing rather than yours, which is exactly why it keeps sliding — and exactly why one call would be unusual enough to matter. Do not read the two passes as a price signal; the objection is square footage.

upcoming: 📭 NOTHING IS BOOKED ANYWHERE ON THE SHOWING CALENDAR — not one confirmed future showing, walk-through, inspection or appraisal in the feed. The last tour of any kind was Thursday lunchtime at 2368 Ridge Trail, and that one has already come back.

⏰ THU 8/28 — 195 LAKE VIEW CIR closes. 🔴 Three items are open with a week to go: survey, home warranty and septic, and the title side has not replied in-thread since 8/20. Septic has lead time, which is what turns a paperwork list into a date risk. The follow-up is already written and staged — send it, don't rewrite it.

📅 SAT 8/30 — 833 MADISON LN goes live. Nothing is booked because it is not on the market yet. ⭐ The Willow Point lesson applies: the gap that costs you is between “photos ready” and “live,” so 8/30 is the date to protect.
📆 MON 9/14 — 3350 ALTAMONT RD E21 closes. All three gates are essentially behind it; the only quiet item is the inspection paperwork sitting with your seller since 8/17.
📆 FRI 10/23 — 1709 FIELDSTONE CIR closes. Longest runway on the board, which makes this the cheapest week to settle the open appraisal question rather than the most expensive one.
